sentences.text:
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section18(3)(b) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereafter referred as L.A.Act) with a prayer to direct the respondent No.1 to make a reference of her application dated 16.09.2010.
.2.

The petition case in nutshell is that the petitioner purchased the portion of schedule property formed in Survey No.60/3A/A from respondent No.2 under a registered sale deed dated 16.04.1994 and the said property bounded with property of Chikkananjappa on East, property of Venkatesh on West, Road by North and remaining land of respondent No.2 on South, measuring East to West 32  feet and North to South 40 feet.

The petitioner further claims L.A.C. No.20/2011 that the said property has been acquired for formation of Metro Rail line through Preliminary Notification dated 31.01.2009 and Final Notification dated 23.02.2010.

The petitioner further claims that when she has purchased the property, the property was in the nature of revenue property and her name was not reflected in RTC and revenue records as it was a revenue site.
Therefore, her name was not found in the notification.

The petitioner further claims that she was totally unaware of the acquisition proceedings and when she came to know about the acquisition proceedings, she has filed the application before the LAO as on 16.09.2010 seeking reference to the Court but the LAO has not made out any reference to the Court.
Hence, filed this petition.
The respondent No.1 though served with the notice of the case not filed any objection statement.

The respondent No.2 filed objection statement wherein he totally denied the petition case with further claiming that he was not an absolute owner of the L.A.C. No.20/2011 property claimed by the petitioner and it is his joint family property.
The respondent No.2 disputed about execution of sale deed in respect of the property claimed by the petitioner.

Further it is claimed by the respondent No.2 that the documents produced by the petitioner discloses that her property is bearing Survey No. 59/1 and among other grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition.
.4. To prove her case, petitioner is examined herself as PW.1 by filing evidence affidavit and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.

The respondents have not chosen to lead any evidence in support of their defence nor got marked the documents.
.5.
On the basis of above, the point for consideration is that.

"Whether the petitioner made out sufficient grounds to issue direction to the respondent No.1- SLAO to make a reference to the Civil Court to decide the market value of the acquired property?"
L.A.C. No.20/2011 .6.

Heard the arguments, petitioner filed written arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis, my finding on the above point is in the negative, for the following:
REASONS .7. Point: Undisputedly this petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 18(3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act seeking direction of the Court to the respondent No.1 to make a reference to the Court of her application dated 16.09.2010.

As this petition is under Section 18(3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act that Komala vs The L A O on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14966242/
2 has been enacted to the Land Acquisition Act by Karnataka State

sentences.text: , the petitioner has to satisfy the Court that her claim for reference is in accordance with Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act.
If the petitioner satisfy all the statutory requirements as contemplated under Section 18(1) to 18(3) of the Land Acquisition Act then only the petition of the petitioner can be allowed.
Hence, the petitioner has to satisfy the L.A.C. No.20/2011 Court that her petition/case will come within the purview of Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act.

In the case on hand, identity of the property is also disputed by the respondent No.2 and the specific claim of the respondent No.2 during the trial as well as in the objection statement is that the property acquired is different from the property claimed by the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has to prove the said fact also.
In the case on hand, either the petitioner or the respondent No.2 were not named either in the Preliminary Notification or Final Notification.

Therefore, the petitioner and the respondent No.2 prima facie failed to make out a case that there was actual dispute between petitioner and the respondent No.2 regarding acquired property or property belongs to them have been acquired or they have been notified in the concerned notifications issued for the acquisition of property.
The nature of the dispute between petitioner and the respondent No.2 appears from pleadings shows that they are disputing the title of each other.

If at all there was a dispute L.A.C.
No.20/2011 regarding title of the property between the petitioner and the respondent No.2 regarding the title, then this petitioner ought to have raised objections by claiming right over the property as contemplated under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act and the petitioner ought to have claimed before the LAO to make a reference to the Court to decide the title over the acquired property as well as apportionment of compensation or at least this petitioner ought to have claimed right over the property before the LAO by producing her title deeds over the acquired property and requested the LAO to decide the title over the property and pay the compensation in respect of the acquired property.
The case on hand is totally different and the dispute between the parties is regarding title, hence seeking reference under Section 18(3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act is certainly not applicable.
In fact, the petitioner ought to have filed declaratory suit against the respondents before the competent Court but it is L.A.C. No.20/2011 otherwise.

As such, it is just and necessary to see Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, which reads as:
"18. Reference to Court (1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:Provided that every such application shall be made,
(a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collectors award;

3 (b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collectors award, whichever period shall first expire.
"(3) (a) The Deputy Commissioner shall, within ninety days from the date of receipt of an application under sub- section (1), make a reference to the Court;
(b) if the Deputy Commissioner does not make a reference to the Court within a period of ninety days from the date of L.A.C. No.20/2011 receipt of the application, the applicant may apply to the Court to direct the Deputy Commissioner to make the reference, and the Court may direct the Deputy Commissioner to make the reference within such time as the Court may fix."
The entire petition averments nowhere discloses that the petitioner is aware of the award passed by the LAO.

sentences.text: Section 18 will be attracted only after passing of the award.

If a party or land looser not satisfy with the award passed by the LAO then only the petitioner can file an application before the LAO under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act seeking reference to the Civil Court either to determine the actual market value of the acquired property or regarding measurement or identity of the property.
Undisputedly this petitioner and the respondent No.2 are not the khathedars of the acquired property and their names were not notified in the respective preliminary and final notifications.

It is also relevant to note that there is no material on record to show that this petitioner has disputed the title of either respondent No.2 or others in respect of the acquired L.A.C.
No.20/2011 property before passing of the award.
Infact the parties have no knowledge of passing of award as per Section 12 of the Land Acquisition Act and there is no pleading either by the petitioner or respondent No.2.
Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act will come into play or will be become active only after passing of the award or service of award notice.
In the case on hand, the petitioner is totally silent about the passing of the award or service of award notice as contemplated under Section 12 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act.
When such is the case certainly this petition under Section 18(3)(b) will not be maintainable as the petitioner is not challenging the award passed by the LAO.
When the award passed by the LAO was not challenged by the parties, certainly this petition is not maintainable.

The primary requirement to file an application under Section 18(3)(b)
of Land Acquisition Act is to challenge the award passed by the LAO.
In fact there is not even a whisper by the petitioner that she is aggrieved by the award passed by the LAO.
As stated earlier the award passed by the LAO L.A.C. No.20/2011 was not under challenge in this petition.

When the award was not under challenged in the petition certainly any application under Section 18(3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act is not maintainable and in fact unless and until the award has been challenged Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act will not come into play.
Therefore, in the aforesaid reasons, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has failed to make out sufficient grounds to direct the respondent No.1 to make a reference to the Court.
Accordingly, the above point is answered in the negative.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/s.18(3)(b) of L.A. Act, 1894 is hereby dismissed.
